title: PMI's head of comms shares why owned content is so important now
excerpt: Moira Gilchrist, chief communications officer at PMI, talks about why she is focusing on strategic owned content in the era of AI
content_html:
A self-described AI "enthusiast," Moira Gilchrist, Philip Morris International's chief global communications officer, said that audience personas the company has created to test its messages have been a valuable application of artificial intelligence.

"Those personas are absolutely fascinating," she said. "The feedback that we get really helps us to improve how we're communicating."

In a video interview with CMO Insider, Gilchrist said that PMI, whose portfolio includes smoke-free brands like Zyn and Iqos, is focusing on optimizing its owned channels, including its corporate website, for large language models.

Gilchrist, who spoke to us after the first quarter of the financial year, also said that PMI is leveraging its internal metrics to demonstrate its ongoing business evolution of replacing cigarettes with smoke-free products.

The following transcript has been edited for length and clarity.

I'm using AI tools for pretty much everything. I'm an absolute enthusiast, maybe an early adopter, and I can't think of a single part of my life where it has no use.

From a work perspective, we've done some pretty exciting stuff to help us understand how our audience thinks and how we can ensure that our messages actually resonate with them.

We've built what I call personas: artificial audience replicas where we can play around with our messaging to make sure that it's actually right for the audience. Those personas are absolutely fascinating. The feedback that we get really helps us to improve how we're communicating.

The company website is more relevant in the AI era

Our corporate website has become an important vehicle for us to set the record straight because large language models are accessing the information that is on there. I think it's going to help us actually rebalance the information ecosystem to make sure that the facts are told correctly. So we've put a much greater emphasis on our own channels as being a strategic communication channel.

It sounds crazy, but before why would you ever go to the PMI website? Nobody would go there, unless you were a journalist or perhaps an investor or something like that. The general public would never go there. But there's a lot of really important information there about our company's transformation, the progress we've made, and the products that we've developed and are selling in hundreds of markets around the world.

I wouldn't say it's a case of more resources. I think it's a more thoughtful approach to our own channels, working to make sure that the LLMs can pick up the information there in the best way possible.

That's an art that everybody's learning today. The days of search engine optimization are over — now it's all about generative engine optimization.

We're making sure that the LLMs can pick up the rich information that's there and serve it up when people are inquiring about us.

Internal data helps tell the transformation story

We realized a couple of years ago that we had to make a better effort to help the world understand the magnitude of the transformation we've already undergone. So we started using some of the metrics we had been using internally much more externally.

We were running a campaign every quarter around our earnings releases that highlights key metrics like the percentage of our net revenues that come from smoke-free alternatives.

When we first launched smoke-free alternatives — the first one in Japan in 2015 — 0% of our net revenues were coming from smoke-free alternatives.

Fast forward to Q1 2026. In the data that we released, 43% of our net revenues come from smoke-free alternatives. So that helps people to understand the magnitude of progress that we've made already.

We still have a long way to go, but I'm super proud of the progress we've made so far.

Erica Iacono is a contributor to Business Insider 

Julia Hood

content_html_zh:
菲利普莫里斯国际公司首席全球传播官莫伊拉·吉尔克里斯特自称人工智能“爱好者”，她表示，该公司为测试其信息而创建的受众角色是人工智能的一个有价值的应用。

“这些角色绝对令人着迷，”她说。 “我们得到的反馈确实有助于我们改善沟通方式。”

Gilchrist 在接受 CMO Insider 视频采访时表示，PMI 的产品组合包括 Zyn 和 Iqos 等无烟品牌，该公司正专注于优化其自有渠道，包括其公司网站，以实现大型语言模型。

Gilchrist 在本财年第一季度后接受我们采访时还表示，PMI 正在利用其内部指标来展示其用无烟产品替代卷烟的持续业务发展。

为了长度和清晰度，以下文字记录已被编辑。

我几乎在所有事情上都使用人工智能工具。 我是一个绝对的爱好者，也许是一个早期采用者，我想不出我生活中的任何一个部分它是没有用的。

从工作角度来看，我们做了一些非常令人兴奋的事情来帮助我们了解受众的想法以及如何确保我们的信息真正引起他们的共鸣。

我们已经构建了我所说的角色：人工受众复制品，我们可以在其中尝试我们的消息，以确保它确实适合受众。 这些人物角色绝对令人着迷。 我们得到的反馈确实有助于我们改进沟通方式。

公司网站在AI时代更具相关性

我们的公司网站已成为我们澄清事实的重要工具，因为大型语言模型正在访问那里的信息。 我认为这将帮助我们真正重新平衡信息生态系统，以确保正确地讲述事实。 因此，我们更加重视我们自己的渠道，将其作为战略沟通渠道。

这听起来很疯狂，但在此之前你为什么要访问 PMI 网站呢？ 没有人会去那里，除非你是记者或者投资者或者类似的人。 一般大众永远不会去那里。 但其中有很多非常重要的信息，涉及我们公司的转型、我们取得的进步以及我们开发的产品并在全球数百个市场销售。

我不会说这是更多资源的情况。 我认为这是对我们自己的渠道更周到的方法，努力确保法学硕士能够以尽可能最好的方式获取信息。

这是今天每个人都在学习的一门艺术。 搜索引擎优化的时代已经结束——现在一切都与生成引擎优化有关。

我们确保法学硕士能够获取那里丰富的信息，并在人们询问我们时提供这些信息。

内部数据有助于讲述转型故事

几年前我们意识到，我们必须做出更好的努力来帮助世界了解我们已经经历的变革的规模。 因此，我们开始更多地在外部使用我们内部一直使用的一些指标。

我们每个季度都会围绕我们的收益发布开展一项活动，突出显示关键指标，例如来自无烟替代品的净收入百分比。

当我们首次推出无烟替代品时（2015 年在日本推出第一款），我们净收入的 0% 来自无烟替代品。

快进到 2026 年第一季度。 在我们发布的数据中，我们 43% 的净收入来自无烟替代品。 这有助于人们了解我们已经取得的进步的幅度。

我们还有很长的路要走，但我对我们迄今为止所取得的进展感到非常自豪。
